summary: This informational memo defines the CRID URL scheme from TV-Anytime, which refers to current or future scheduled broadcast media content over television platforms and the Internet. A CRID can be embedded as a link in schedule information.

eli5.summary: Instead of naming a show by channel and time, a CRID names the programme itself, so you can find it however it is shown.

questions: how do i resolve a crid
subtitle: A URL scheme that identifies broadcast programs independently of when or where they air.

tldr.problem: Television and radio programs are shown at different times and on different platforms, making it hard to link program information to where a viewer can actually find it.
tldr.mechanism: CRID defines a URL scheme using domain names and identifiers to name programs, so the same program can be referenced no matter where or when it airs.
tldr.outcome: Viewers and recording devices can link program metadata to all the places and times a program is broadcast.

today: RFC 4078 is an Informational RFC that documents the TV-Anytime CRID specification. It is not obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: What CRID Does
sections.content: The TV-Anytime standard defined a URL scheme called CRID (Content Reference Identifier) to solve a problem in broadcast television and radio. As people gain access to programs through satellite, cable, terrestrial broadcast and the Internet, the same program appears at many different times and places. Programme metadata (information about a show, its cast, plot, and so on) might describe a program without saying when or where to actually find it. CRID bridges that gap by naming the program itself, allowing metadata to be linked to all the places and times it is broadcast.
sections.eli5: CRID is like naming a movie instead of saying 'Channel 5 at 8pm.' That way you can find it whenever it plays.

sections.title: CRID Syntax
sections.content:
A CRID is a URL with the format crid://<domain>/<data>. The domain part is a registered Internet domain name that identifies the authority who created the CRID. The data part is any string meaningful to that authority, following the rules of RFC 3986 URIs. For example, crid://example.com/show-123 names a program managed by example.com with identifier show-123.

The entire CRID must be URI-compliant. Characters outside the normal URI range must be encoded as UTF-8 and escaped with percent signs. For instance, a CRID might reference content using KATAKANA Japanese characters: crid://example.co.jp/%E3%82%A8%E3%82%A4%E3%82%AC.
sections.eli5: A CRID looks like a web address: the domain part says who created it, and the rest is a code that means something to that company.

sections.title: How CRIDs Work
sections.content:
CRID is designed as a bridge. On one side is programme metadata in tables that list program information. On the other side are locators that tell a device where to find the program (the channel and time for a broadcast, or a URL for Internet delivery). The CRID connects them. A single CRID can point to multiple locators because the same program is often broadcast repeatedly or on multiple platforms.

The CRID authority can also create higher-level CRIDs that group related programs. For example, all episodes of a series might be grouped under one CRID, while each episode has its own CRID. The metadata system specified by TV-Anytime describes how these relationships are stored.
sections.eli5: A CRID connects the description of a show to all the times and places it airs. One CRID can point to the same show on many channels at many times.

sections.title: Resolving and Using CRIDs
sections.content:
To use a CRID, a device reads the CRID from program metadata and asks the CRID authority (or another trusted resolver) to provide the locator information needed to find the program. This resolution process is dynamic: broadcasters can update the locators right up to air time if schedules change, allowing for last-minute adjustments in a live broadcast service. The resolution happens at the time a viewer or agent needs it, not in advance.

Note that the CRID scheme uses registered domain names, but does not require use of the Domain Name System for resolution. The TV-Anytime specification describes the exact resolution mechanism, which operates independently.
sections.eli5: When you want to watch a show, you ask the CRID authority 'where is this program tonight?' and they tell you the channel and time.
